text:
Maria L: Heads-up, memory-first incident on prod-gpu-pool-2, ~3% p50 tail OOMs since the 04:00 deploy. saw kernel choice flip to fast-attn-v2 on long sequences :confused:
Alex P: Ugh. did the deploy change kernel-auto?
Maria L: yeah, autotuner now prefers fast-attn-v2 for speed but it's using more workspace for long seqs. KV cache pressure + larger workspace = hairball.
CJ: timeline? small spike at 04:12 then periodic at 04:17/04:33 etc, correlates with batch sizes hitting 8->12 when requests burst.
Darren: sounds like combined problem: kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV retention. we should run an incident playbook decision tree instead of ad-hoc fixes.
Maria L: proposed quick mitigations: 1) force kernel fallback to stable-attn-1 for >1024 tokens 2) clamp batch size to 8 for the pool 3) enable KV snapshot-to-cpu for idle sessions 4) if memory >85% trigger circuit-breaker that returns 503+Retry-After
Alex P: can we do 3) quickly? snapshotting small KV spans to host RAM or pinned CPU pagecache would be the fastest to roll out AFAIK.
CJ: repo has snapshot code but it's gated behind flag `--kv-snapshot-to-host`. toggle in runtime config, no build required. command: `curl -X POST $CONTROL/api/pools/prod-gpu-pool-2/config -d '{"kv_snapshot": "host"}'`
Darren: also add a temporary request-slimmer middleware to reduce max tokens per request to 1024 and reduce echo tokens by 25% for embeddings/long-completions. low-risk config change.
Maria L: oncall, please run steps in order: a) enable kv snapshot to host b) clamp max_batch_size=8 c) patch kernel selector policy: prefer stable-attn for seq>1024 d) enable circuit-breaker threshold at 85% GPU memory.
Oncall-Bot: @Oncall accepted incident. Runbook link: https://intra.redwood/plays/oom-decision-tree
InfraBot: rolling config to prod-gpu-pool-2: step a) in progress... :gear:  (eta ~30s)
InfraBot: step a) complete. KV snapshotting enabled and background flush frequency set to 15s.
Alex P: monitorable: `gpu_mem_used_pct`, `kv_host_evictions`, `batch_size_distribution`, `kernel_selector_choice`. dashboards are updated.
CJ: after a) we saw immediate drop in allocation spikes but still occasional 1-2 OOMs at 04:28. proceeding to b).
InfraBot: step b) applied: max_batch_size=8 on prod-gpu-pool-2.
Maria L: good. if OOMs persist after b) then fallback to stable-attn policy and enable minibatch-probing to avoid coldstart peak.
Darren: c) applied manually via `PATCH /control/config/kernel_policy` with body `{ "policy": "stable_for_long_seq" }`. note: this will slightly increase latency for some short seq paths.
Alex P: telemetry shows kernel selector flips decreased from 40% to 5% variance. memory headroom rose ~6%.
CJ: still seeing a couple of late failures tied to long-lived sessions with large KV. suggestion: snapshot + trim KV TTL aggressively for idle sessions (TTL->30s) and enable async reclaim.
Maria L: let's do aggressive KV TTL for idle=30s as a short-term. also add a mitigation: on OOM attempt, runtime should try 3-step rollback: 1) evict oldest KV spans 2) if insufficient, downgrade kernel 3) if still OOM, reject with graceful 503 and include `x-fallback-model: small-quant` header.
Darren: we should document that as an opaque decision tree. I'll draft a mini-playbook and add the rollback pseudo-code:
Darren: ```
if gpu_mem_pct > 90%:
  evict_kv(oldest_spans=100)
  wait 50ms
  if gpu_mem_pct still > 90%:
    switch_kernel(target=stable-quantized)
    wait 20ms
    if still >90%:
      return 503 with Retry-After and header x-fallback-model: small-quant
```
CJ: + add metric `oom_rollback_stage` with labels `evict`,`kernel_switch`,`reject` to track which branch fires.
InfraBot: applied TTL change for idle KV to 30s and enabled async_reclaim flag.
Oncall-Bot: Monitoring: annotate incident at 04:52 and notify #eng-runtime-incident-log.
Maria L: immediate outcome: after steps a-c + TTL, OOMs dropped to zero in last 20m. p50 latency up 12ms on smallest requests, acceptable.
Alex P: next actions: 1) bake autotuner with workspace constraints (no kernel recommended that needs >X% workspace) 2) add kernel cost model into selector 3) long-term: KV spill to local SSD for very large sessions 4) add automated canary for kernel selection changes
CJ: I'll generate profiling snapshot for the problematic trace and attach to the playbook. snippet for capturing profile: `rdw profile capture --pool prod-gpu-pool-2 --trace 04:12-04:40 --out s3://rdw-profiles/2612345678.json`
Maria L: thanks. draft saved to runbook. great response team. :heart:
Darren: we should convert this ad-hoc thread into a permanent incident playbook: "OOM decision tree with KV snapshotting & rollback". I'll PR to infra-playbooks repo.
Oncall-Bot: incident closed by @Oncall. Summary: kernel autotuner regression -> higher workspace usage -> batch burst -> KV pressure; mitigated by KV snapshot-to-host, batch clamp, kernel fallback policy, aggressive KV TTL, eviction+rollback flow.
InfraBot: deploy notes: rollback toggles are now feature-flagged for safer rollouts.
Maria L: postmortem items: - add kernel workspace estimation to perf profiles - bake cost model - canary every kernel selector change - automated rollback metric `oom_rollback_stage`. I'll assign owners in the PM doc.
Alex P: great job everyone. follow-up meeting in 60m to convert to playbook.
